definition: Short for "to be honest"; introduces a frank opinion or admission.
example: tbh I did not study at all.
exampleTranslation: To be honest, I did not study at all.
context: Common in texts, chats and social posts; usually too casual for formal writing.

definition: Short for "in my opinion"; marks a statement as personal view.
example: imo the book was better than the movie.
exampleTranslation: In my opinion, the book was better than the movie.
context: Common in texts, chats and social posts; usually too casual for formal writing.

definition: Short for "in my humble opinion"; a slightly softer or sometimes sarcastic version of IMO.
example: imho, pineapple belongs on pizza.
exampleTranslation: In my humble opinion, pineapple belongs on pizza.
context: Common in texts, chats and social posts; usually too casual for formal writing.
era: Common since early internet forums and email, approx. 1990s
mistakes: The "humble" is often ironic, so it can sound smug rather than modest.

definition: Short for "I don't know."
example: idk what time practice starts.
exampleTranslation: I do not know what time practice starts.
context: Common in texts, chats and social posts; usually too casual for formal writing.

definition: Short for "I don't care"; can mean real indifference or "I'm fine with either."
example: idc where we eat, you pick.
exampleTranslation: I do not care where we eat; you pick.
context: Common in texts, chats and social posts; usually too casual for formal writing.
mistakes: Can sound cold or dismissive in text even when meant casually.

definition: Short for "I know, right?"; used to agree enthusiastically.
example: ikr, that quiz was so hard!
exampleTranslation: I know, right? That quiz was so hard!
context: Common in texts, chats and social posts; usually too casual for formal writing.

definition: Short for "not gonna lie"; signals a candid statement.
example: ngl, that song is catchy.
exampleTranslation: Not going to lie, that song is catchy.
context: Common in texts, chats and social posts; usually too casual for formal writing.

definition: Short for "right now."
example: im at the library rn.
exampleTranslation: I am at the library right now.
context: Common in texts, chats and social posts; usually too casual for formal writing.
mistakes: Also a common abbreviation for "registered nurse," so context matters.

definition: Short for "in real life"; contrasts offline life with online.
example: we met online but irl we live close.
exampleTranslation: We met online, but in real life we live close.
context: Common in texts, chats and social posts; usually too casual for formal writing.
era: Common since early chat rooms and forums, approx. 1990s

definition: Short for "away from keyboard"; means the person is not at their device.
example: afk for ten minutes, dinner time.
exampleTranslation: Away from keyboard for ten minutes; it is dinner time.
context: Used in chats and especially online games to say you have stepped away.
origin: Early chat rooms and online games, approx. 1990s

definition: Short for "be right back."
example: brb, grabbing a snack.
exampleTranslation: Be right back, I am grabbing a snack.
context: Common in texts, chats and social posts; usually too casual for formal writing.

definition: Short for "by the way"; adds a side note.
example: btw, practice moved to Thursday.
exampleTranslation: By the way, practice moved to Thursday.
context: Common in texts, chats and social posts; usually too casual for formal writing.

definition: A private message sent on a social app; as a verb, to message someone privately. "Slide into the DMs" means to start a private chat, often a bit boldly.
meanings: "Slide into someone's DMs": message a person you do not know well, sometimes with romantic interest.
example: dm me the link when you find it.
exampleTranslation: Send me the link in a private message when you find it.
context: Used on Instagram, X, TikTok, Discord and similar apps. The "slide into DMs" phrase can imply flirting.

definition: The "For You" page on TikTok, a personalized feed. "On my FYP" means the algorithm showed it to me.
meanings: Used as a hashtag (#fyp) in hopes a video gets recommended widely.
example: this cat video keeps showing up on my fyp.
exampleTranslation: This cat video keeps showing up on my For You page.
context: Common in texts, chats and social posts; usually too casual for formal writing.
origin: TikTok

definition: "Point of view." On video apps it introduces a skit or scene told from one character's perspective, often "POV: you are..."
meanings: In ordinary writing, simply "point of view" or the viewpoint of a story narrator.
example: pov: your teacher says the test is open book.
exampleTranslation: Imagine this from your perspective: your teacher says the test is open book.
context: Common in texts, chats and social posts; usually too casual for formal writing.
era: Meme format popularized on short-video apps, approx. late 2010s–2020s

definition: "One of my followers" (sometimes "one of my mutuals"); used to refer to someone you vaguely know online without naming them.
example: oomf just posted the funniest meme.
exampleTranslation: One of my followers just posted the funniest meme.
context: Common in texts, chats and social posts; usually too casual for formal writing.

definition: Short for "at this point"; expresses resignation or a conclusion.
example: atp I will just order pizza.
exampleTranslation: At this point I will just order pizza.
context: Common in texts, chats and social posts; usually too casual for formal writing.
mistakes: Also the name of a chemical (adenosine triphosphate) in science class.

definition: Short for "I swear to God"; stresses frustration or sincerity.
example: istg if the wifi cuts out again...
exampleTranslation: I swear to God, if the wifi cuts out again...
context: Common in texts, chats and social posts; usually too casual for formal writing.
sensitiveNote: Expands to a mild religious oath; some families and schools prefer it avoided.

definition: "Too much information"; said when someone shares more personal detail than you wanted.
example: tmi, I did not need to hear about your breakfast.
exampleTranslation: Too much information; I did not need to hear about your breakfast.
context: Common in texts, chats and social posts; usually too casual for formal writing.

definition: "Too long; didn't read"; a short summary of a long post, or a comment that something is too long.
meanings: Said of a long text as "tl;dr" meaning "I did not read all that."
example: tl;dr: the meeting moved to 3 p.m.
exampleTranslation: In short: the meeting moved to 3 p.m.
context: Common in texts, chats and social posts; usually too casual for formal writing.
origin: Internet forums, approx. 2000s

definition: "Where you at?" asking someone's location.
example: wya? we are outside.
exampleTranslation: Where are you? We are outside.
context: Common in texts, chats and social posts; usually too casual for formal writing.

definition: "What you doing?" a casual check-in or conversation starter.
example: wyd after school?
exampleTranslation: What are you doing after school?
context: Common in texts, chats and social posts; usually too casual for formal writing.

definition: "What's the word?" a greeting or a request for the plan. Sometimes used with "what's the wave."
example: wtw tonight, anyone free?
exampleTranslation: What is the plan tonight, anyone free?
context: Common in texts, chats and social posts; usually too casual for formal writing.
sensitiveNote: Sometimes read as a different, ruder phrase beginning with "what the"; context decides. Usually harmless.
mistakes: Easily confused with "WTF" or "what the..." phrases; check context.

definition: "How about you?" a quick way to return a question.
example: im good, hbu?
exampleTranslation: I am good, how about you?
context: Common in texts, chats and social posts; usually too casual for formal writing.

definition: "Let me know."
example: lmk if you can come Saturday.
exampleTranslation: Let me know if you can come Saturday.
context: Common in texts, chats and social posts; usually too casual for formal writing.

definition: "Shaking my head"; shows disapproval or disbelief.
example: he forgot his own birthday, smh.
exampleTranslation: He forgot his own birthday, shaking my head.
context: Common in texts, chats and social posts; usually too casual for formal writing.

definition: "Hit me up"; contact me.
example: hmu if you want to study together.
exampleTranslation: Contact me if you want to study together.
context: Common in texts, chats and social posts; usually too casual for formal writing.

definition: "If you know, you know"; refers to an inside joke or reference only some people get.
example: that cafeteria pizza though, iykyk.
exampleTranslation: That cafeteria pizza, though. If you know, you know.
context: Common in texts, chats and social posts; usually too casual for formal writing.
mistakes: Using it for something everyone knows defeats the point.

definition: Anxiety that others are having fun or opportunities without you.
example: I stayed on my phone all night out of fomo.
exampleTranslation: I stayed on my phone all night out of fear of missing out.
context: Common in texts, chats and social posts; usually too casual for formal writing.

definition: "Profile picture," the small image that represents an account.
example: new pfp, do you like it?
exampleTranslation: New profile picture, do you like it?
context: Common in texts, chats and social posts; usually too casual for formal writing.

definition: "Laughing out loud"; today often just a light, friendly softener.
meanings: Often used as a filler to soften a message, without real laughter.
example: lol that was so unexpected.
exampleTranslation: Ha, that was so unexpected.
context: Common in texts, chats and social posts; usually too casual for formal writing.

definition: "Laughing my a-- off"; stronger than LOL.
example: lmao the dog stole my sandwich.
exampleTranslation: I am laughing hard; the dog stole my sandwich.
context: Common in texts, chats and social posts; usually too casual for formal writing.
sensitiveNote: Contains a mild swear word when spelled out; LMFAO is stronger.

definition: "Rolling on the floor laughing"; strong laughter.
example: rofl that prank was perfect.
exampleTranslation: I am rolling on the floor laughing; that prank was perfect.
context: Common in texts, chats and social posts; usually too casual for formal writing.
era: Popular on early internet chat, approx. 1990s–2000s

definition: "Oh my God"; reaction to surprise or excitement.
example: omg you got tickets!
exampleTranslation: Oh my gosh, you got tickets!
context: Common in texts, chats and social posts; usually too casual for formal writing.
sensitiveNote: Some people consider it an irreverent use of a religious phrase; "oh my gosh" is a gentler swap.

definition: "In case you missed it"; introduces something worth catching up on.
example: icymi, the game is moved to Friday.
exampleTranslation: In case you missed it, the game is moved to Friday.
context: Common in texts, chats and social posts; usually too casual for formal writing.

definition: "Never mind."
example: nvm, I found my keys.
exampleTranslation: Never mind, I found my keys.
context: Common in texts, chats and social posts; usually too casual for formal writing.

definition: "Talk to you later."
example: ttyl, class is starting.
exampleTranslation: Talk to you later, class is starting.
context: Common in texts, chats and social posts; usually too casual for formal writing.

definition: "Got to go"; ends a chat.
example: gtg, mom is calling.
exampleTranslation: I have to go, my mom is calling.
context: Common in texts, chats and social posts; usually too casual for formal writing.

definition: "Just kidding."
example: I ate your cookie. jk, it is safe.
exampleTranslation: I ate your cookie. Just kidding, it is safe.
context: Common in texts, chats and social posts; usually too casual for formal writing.

definition: "I love you"; used between family, friends and partners.
example: ily mom, see you tonight.
exampleTranslation: I love you, Mom; see you tonight.
context: Common in texts, chats and social posts; usually too casual for formal writing.

definition: "I love you too."
example: ily2, have a great day!
exampleTranslation: I love you too; have a great day!
context: Common in texts, chats and social posts; usually too casual for formal writing.

definition: "Best friends forever"; a very close friend.
example: she is my bff since second grade.
exampleTranslation: She is my best friend and has been since second grade.
context: Common in texts, chats and social posts; usually too casual for formal writing.

definition: "One true pairing"; a fictional couple a fan most wants together. Also used loosely for any ideal pair.
example: my otp from that show finally kissed.
exampleTranslation: My favorite couple from that show finally kissed.
context: Common in texts, chats and social posts; usually too casual for formal writing.
origin: Fan fiction communities, approx. 2000s
mistakes: OTP also means "one-time password" in tech.

definition: Marks content that may be adult or inappropriate to open at work or school.
example: that link is nsfw, do not open it here.
exampleTranslation: That link is not safe for work; do not open it here.
context: Common in texts, chats and social posts; usually too casual for formal writing.
sensitiveNote: A content warning label, not itself explicit; it signals adult material follows.

definition: "For the win"; cheering something on.
example: pizza friday ftw!
exampleTranslation: Pizza Friday is the best!
context: Common in texts, chats and social posts; usually too casual for formal writing.
mistakes: Some people read it as a rude phrase; the intended meaning here is "for the win."

definition: "You only live once"; a rationale for a bold or risky choice.
example: yolo, I tried the spicy ramen.
exampleTranslation: You only live once; I tried the spicy ramen.
context: Common in texts, chats and social posts; usually too casual for formal writing.
origin: Popularized in the early 2010s partly through hip-hop lyrics

definition: "That feeling when"; starts a relatable situation.
example: tfw you find money in an old jacket.
exampleTranslation: That feeling when you find money in an old jacket.
context: Common in texts, chats and social posts; usually too casual for formal writing.
era: Meme format from imageboards, approx. early 2010s

definition: "My face when"; paired with a reaction image or description.
example: mfw the bell rings early.
exampleTranslation: My face when the bell rings early.
context: Common in texts, chats and social posts; usually too casual for formal writing.

definition: "If I remember correctly."
example: iirc, the test is Monday.
exampleTranslation: If I remember correctly, the test is Monday.
context: Common in texts, chats and social posts; usually too casual for formal writing.

definition: "Outfit of the day"; a photo or post showing what someone is wearing.
example: ootd: new sneakers and a jean jacket.
exampleTranslation: Outfit of the day: new sneakers and a jean jacket.
context: Common in texts, chats and social posts; usually too casual for formal writing.

definition: "Thank you so much."
example: tysm for helping me move!
exampleTranslation: Thank you so much for helping me move!
context: Common in texts, chats and social posts; usually too casual for formal writing.

definition: "No problem."
example: np, happy to help.
exampleTranslation: No problem, happy to help.
context: Common in texts, chats and social posts; usually too casual for formal writing.

definition: "Of course."
example: ofc I will save you a seat.
exampleTranslation: Of course I will save you a seat.
context: Common in texts, chats and social posts; usually too casual for formal writing.

definition: "Thank you."
example: ty for the ride!
exampleTranslation: Thank you for the ride!
context: Common in texts, chats and social posts; usually too casual for formal writing.

definition: "I don't even know"; shows confusion or being overwhelmed.
example: idek what is going on in this group chat.
exampleTranslation: I do not even know what is going on in this group chat.
context: Common in texts, chats and social posts; usually too casual for formal writing.

definition: Skull emoji used to mean something is so funny that the sender is "dead."
example: He fell off his chair 💀
exampleTranslation: He fell off his chair and it is hilarious.
context: Common in texts, chats and social posts; usually too casual for formal writing.
mistakes: Taken literally it looks grim; context shows the joke. Not used for real tragedies.

definition: Loudly-crying emoji used for exaggerated laughter or being overwhelmed by something cute, funny or relatable, rather than sadness.
plain: I am laughing so hard / that is so sweet
example: he did the dance perfectly 😭
exampleTranslation: He did the dance perfectly and I am overcome.
context: Common in texts, chats and social posts; usually too casual for formal writing.
mistakes: Can mean real sadness too; tone and topic matter.

definition: Billed-cap emoji used to say someone is lying or exaggerating (from "cap" meaning lie).
example: you ran a mile in two minutes 🧢
exampleTranslation: You are lying about running a mile in two minutes.
context: Common in texts, chats and social posts; usually too casual for formal writing.
origin: Visual shorthand for "cap," slang from AAVE and hip-hop communities meaning to lie
mistakes: Do not confuse with a plain hat emoji.

definition: Fire emoji used to praise something as excellent or impressive.
meanings: Sometimes just means literal fire or heat.
example: new track 🔥
exampleTranslation: New track, it is awesome.
context: Common in texts, chats and social posts; usually too casual for formal writing.

definition: Goat emoji used as visual shorthand for GOAT, "greatest of all time."
example: that save 🐐
exampleTranslation: That save was the best of all time.
context: Common in texts, chats and social posts; usually too casual for formal writing.
mistakes: Can also literally mean a goat.

definition: Eyes emoji meaning "I'm watching this," "interesting," or "look at that," often hinting at drama or a hint.
example: new season announced 👀
exampleTranslation: A new season was announced and I am paying attention.
context: Common in texts, chats and social posts; usually too casual for formal writing.

definition: "Good game"; a sportsmanlike thing to say at the end of a match, win or lose. Can also mean "it's over" when said mid-match.
meanings: Mid-game, "gg" can mean the outcome is decided or someone has lost.
example: gg, that was a close one.
exampleTranslation: Good game, that was a close one.
context: Used in online games, voice chat and streams; meaning depends on the game and community.
origin: Online and competitive gaming culture, approx. 1990s

definition: "Good game, easy"; used to taunt a defeated opponent. Seen as poor sportsmanship.
example: he typed gg ez after winning.
exampleTranslation: He taunted us by saying "good game, easy" after winning.
context: Used in online games, voice chat and streams; meaning depends on the game and community.
sensitiveNote: Considered taunting, and many games filter it as unsportsmanlike behavior.

definition: A new or unskilled player; can be a friendly label or an insult.
example: I am a noob at this game, be gentle.
exampleTranslation: I am a beginner at this game, be gentle.
context: Used in online games, voice chat and streams; meaning depends on the game and community.
origin: Gaming and forum culture, derived from "newbie"
mistakes: Said to a beginner in a mean way it can be hurtful.

definition: A player who takes a casual game extremely seriously. "Sweaty" describes such play.
example: this lobby is so sweaty.
exampleTranslation: This group is playing extremely seriously.
context: Used in online games, voice chat and streams; meaning depends on the game and community.

definition: Someone trying very hard, especially at a game, sometimes more than needed.
example: my cousin is such a tryhard in Mario Kart.
exampleTranslation: My cousin takes Mario Kart much too seriously.
context: Used in online games, voice chat and streams; meaning depends on the game and community.

definition: To make a character, weapon or ability less powerful in an update.
example: they nerfed the sniper rifle.
exampleTranslation: They weakened the sniper rifle.
context: Used in online games, voice chat and streams; meaning depends on the game and community.
origin: Gaming; likely from the soft foam Nerf toys, meaning something made harmless

definition: To make a character, weapon or ability more powerful in an update.
meanings: In general talk, "buff" also means muscular.
example: they buffed the healer so she is great now.
exampleTranslation: They strengthened the healer so she is great now.
context: Used in online games, voice chat and streams; meaning depends on the game and community.
origin: MMO and online game culture

definition: In games, so strong it is unfair. Elsewhere, "OP" also means "original poster," the person who started a thread.
meanings: Original poster: the person who made a forum or social media post.
example: that sword is totally OP.
exampleTranslation: That sword is totally overpowered.
context: Used in online games, voice chat and streams; meaning depends on the game and community.
mistakes: Check context: gaming chat means overpowered; forums mean original poster.

definition: Performing very well under pressure, especially winning a tough situation at the last moment.
meanings: Also used in sports.
example: she made a clutch play in overtime.
exampleTranslation: She made a game-saving play in overtime.
context: Used in online games, voice chat and streams; meaning depends on the game and community.

definition: Very good at a game, impressive in a way that seems almost unfair. "Cracked aim" means excellent aiming.
example: he is cracked at this shooter.
exampleTranslation: He is extremely skilled at this shooter.
context: Used in online games, voice chat and streams; meaning depends on the game and community.
mistakes: In other settings "cracked" can mean broken or insane.

definition: To be the main reason a team wins, covering for weaker teammates. "Hard carry" means doing so heavily.
example: you carried us this whole match.
exampleTranslation: You led us to victory this whole match.
context: Used in online games, voice chat and streams; meaning depends on the game and community.
origin: MOBA and team game culture

definition: Staying near where opponents reappear to defeat them again and again.
example: they spawn camped us the whole round.
exampleTranslation: They kept attacking us as we reappeared the whole round.
context: Used in online games, voice chat and streams; meaning depends on the game and community.
origin: Shooter and multiplayer game culture

definition: Intentionally annoying or sabotaging other players, such as destroying their builds or blocking teammates.
example: a griefer wrecked our Minecraft house.
exampleTranslation: A player who spoils others' fun wrecked our Minecraft house.
context: Used in online games, voice chat and streams; meaning depends on the game and community.
origin: Online games from approx. late 1990s–2000s
sensitiveNote: Describes harassment behavior; kid-friendly but unkind.

definition: To abruptly leave a game out of frustration.
example: he rage quit when he lost.
exampleTranslation: He quit in anger when he lost.
context: Used in online games, voice chat and streams; meaning depends on the game and community.

definition: A teasing way to say a problem is due to lack of skill, not the game.
example: that boss is not unfair, it is a skill issue.
exampleTranslation: That boss is not unfair; you just need more practice.
context: Used in online games, voice chat and streams; meaning depends on the game and community.
mistakes: Can sound mean if used on a real struggle.

definition: Short for "difference"; blames a loss on a player or role being better. "Jungle diff" means the jungler made the difference.
example: we lost, mid diff.
exampleTranslation: We lost; the middle player was clearly better.
context: Used in online games, voice chat and streams; meaning depends on the game and community.
origin: League of Legends and MOBA culture

definition: The most effective or popular strategies at a given time in a game. From "metagame."
meanings: Also a trendy word meaning self-referential.
example: the current meta is all about speed.
exampleTranslation: The most effective strategy right now is all about speed.
context: Used in online games, voice chat and streams; meaning depends on the game and community.

definition: Completing a video game as quickly as possible, often using tricks.
meanings: Used jokingly for anything done very fast.
plain: finish a game as fast as possible
example: she speedran the whole game in an hour.
exampleTranslation: She finished the whole game as fast as possible in an hour.
context: Used in online games, voice chat and streams; meaning depends on the game and community.

definition: Cheer for something exciting or impressive. From the Twitch emote PogChamp.
meanings: Possibly connected to the shape of the surprised face in the emote.
example: pog, you beat the level!
exampleTranslation: Awesome, you beat the level!
context: Used in online games, voice chat and streams; meaning depends on the game and community.
origin: Twitch chat; PogChamp emote, popularized approx. 2010s

definition: Ask to save a short video of a great (or funny) moment so it can be shared.
meanings: Used by streamers and viewers.
example: clip that, it was unreal!
exampleTranslation: Save that moment, it was unreal!
context: Used in online games, voice chat and streams; meaning depends on the game and community.

definition: From games where you "unlock" things; used jokingly: "new fear unlocked."
example: new fear unlocked: the haunted house.
exampleTranslation: I just discovered a new fear: the haunted house.
context: Used in online games, voice chat and streams; meaning depends on the game and community.

definition: A small optional task apart from the main goal; used in daily life for small detours.
meanings: Also used for a fun distraction from your main goals.
example: my side quest today: buy stickers.
exampleTranslation: My extra task today: buy stickers.
context: Used in online games, voice chat and streams; meaning depends on the game and community.

definition: The central story mission of a game; in life, your most important task.
example: focus, homework is the main quest.
exampleTranslation: Focus; homework is the main task.
context: Used in online games, voice chat and streams; meaning depends on the game and community.

definition: The last, hardest opponent in a game; used for the toughest obstacle or person ("final boss of homework").
meanings: Sometimes used for the most impressive person at something.
example: algebra is the final boss of my week.
exampleTranslation: Algebra is the toughest challenge of my week.
context: Used in online games, voice chat and streams; meaning depends on the game and community.

definition: Waiting in one spot, usually hidden, to ambush opponents; considered annoying by some.
meanings: Normal use of "camping" also applies; context matters.
example: a sniper camped on the roof.
exampleTranslation: A sniper stayed hidden on the roof waiting to attack.
context: Used in online games, voice chat and streams; meaning depends on the game and community.

definition: An experienced player who makes a new account to play against weaker players.
plain: skilled player on a new account
example: he is a smurf, he is way too good.
exampleTranslation: He is an experienced player on a fresh account, he is far too good.
context: Used in online games, voice chat and streams; meaning depends on the game and community.
origin: Likely from the Smurfs cartoon; competitive games

definition: A delay between your action and what happens on screen because of a slow connection or device.
meanings: Also used for general slowness or falling behind.
example: sorry, I lagged out.
exampleTranslation: Sorry, my connection slowed and I got disconnected.
context: Used in online games, voice chat and streams; meaning depends on the game and community.

definition: A measure of network delay, in milliseconds; "high ping" means a slow connection. Also to send a quick notification.
meanings: "Ping me" at work means send a message.
example: my ping is 300, I keep rubber-banding.
exampleTranslation: My connection is slow, I keep jumping around.
context: Used in online games, voice chat and streams; meaning depends on the game and community.

definition: Upset after a mistake or loss so that your play gets worse.
example: I am on tilt after that loss.
exampleTranslation: I am frustrated and playing badly after that loss.
context: Used in online games, voice chat and streams; meaning depends on the game and community.
origin: Poker, then adopted by online games

definition: Short for "easy"; also used to taunt.
meanings: Can sound like a taunt when said to opponents.
example: that level was ez.
exampleTranslation: That level was easy.
context: Used in online games, voice chat and streams; meaning depends on the game and community.

definition: A relatable or funny thing that happens to a gamer, like a silly mistake.
example: I fell off the map, gamer moment.
exampleTranslation: I fell off the map, a typical gaming mistake.
context: Used in online games, voice chat and streams; meaning depends on the game and community.

definition: Using an easy exploit or silly strategy that beats the game or opponent.
meanings: In other places "cheesy" means corny.
example: he cheesed the boss with a glitch.
exampleTranslation: He beat the boss using an unfair trick.
context: Used in online games, voice chat and streams; meaning depends on the game and community.

definition: "Random number generator"; the luck element in games.
example: rng gave me the rare drop!
exampleTranslation: Random luck gave me the rare drop!
context: Used in online games, voice chat and streams; meaning depends on the game and community.

definition: Repeating tasks to gain levels or items; also working hard in life.
meanings: "The grind" in life means hard work.
example: I am grinding to reach level 50.
exampleTranslation: I am repeating tasks to reach level 50.
context: Used in online games, voice chat and streams; meaning depends on the game and community.

definition: Items gathered by defeating enemies or exploring.
meanings: Loot box: randomized rewards, sometimes bought with money.
example: I got epic loot from the chest.
exampleTranslation: I got great items from the chest.
context: Used in online games, voice chat and streams; meaning depends on the game and community.

definition: A match with one player versus one player. "1v1 me" is a challenge to fight.
example: 1v1 me in the arena!
exampleTranslation: Challenge me to a one-on-one match in the arena!
context: Used in online games, voice chat and streams; meaning depends on the game and community.

definition: To come back after being defeated.
example: I respawned at the base.
exampleTranslation: I reappeared at the base.
context: Used in online games, voice chat and streams; meaning depends on the game and community.

definition: A cheat that aims automatically; accused of players who are too accurate.
example: that player must be using an aimbot.
exampleTranslation: That player must be using cheat software for aiming.
context: Used in online games, voice chat and streams; meaning depends on the game and community.
mistakes: Calling someone an aimbot accuses them of cheating; it may be unfair.

definition: In games, someone using cheats; "hacker!" is shouted at suspiciously good players.
meanings: Outside games, a hacker breaks into computer systems.
example: he is a hacker, no way he saw me!
